utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in session. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon everyone in the courtroom. Good afternoon. This is the case number IT-01-42-A, The Prosecutor versus Pavle Strugar. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Strugar, are you in a position to hear and follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can be seated. I'm now turning to the parties. Can I have the appearances, starting with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Xavier Tracol, appeals attorney; Helen Brady, senior appeals attorney; and Mr. Sebastiaan Van Hooydonk, who is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tracol. Let me now turn to the Defence representatives, the counsel representing Mr. Strugar in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of the Defence of Mr. Strugar, we have Goran Rodic and Vladimir Petrovic appearing as his Defence counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In this case, pending the appeal judgment, Mr. Strugar has been in custody in the United Nations Detention Unit in The Hague, in the Netherlands. Pursuant to the provisions of Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, a Status Conference, an Appeals Status Conference, is convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference in order to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto. In the instant case, the first Status Conference was held on the 1st of October, 2007. The Scheduling Order for this Status Conference was issued on the 14th of January, 2008, and we decided on this date, today, on account of the availability of the Defence counsel. So, Mr. Strugar, I wish to ask you if you have any concern you'd like to express to me regarding detention conditions or your mental and physical condition. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please turn on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as my health is concerned, it is unchanged. I am taking medicines regularly, so it is a status quo, just like I said the last time. As for my conditions in the detention unit, I'm satisfied and have I no problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Mr. Strugar. You can sit down, if you're finished. I note that you do not have any specific complaint. Therefore, with regard to the status of the appeals file, I remind that the Prosecutor filed an addendum to their brief on the 1st of October, 2007, and I also observe that failing any pending motions, the briefing on appeal is now complete and up to date. Pursuant to Rule 114, the Appeals Chamber set the date for the hearing for the date of the 23rd of April, 2008. I refer to an order that also gives the scheduling for the appeals hearing. Should the Appeals Chamber have any specific questions on points that need clarification, the parties will be so informed and notified in due time and place. We have taken good note of what Mr. Strugar told us with regard to his health which has remained unchanged, and he is receiving treatment in the detention unit. Therefore, after saying this, I'll turn, once again, to the parties to ask them whether they have any observations or questions to raise. As far as I'm concerned, indeed I, have no other items I would like to deal with during this Status Conference. Yes, Mr. Tracol.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution wishes to thank you for informing the parties through the Scheduling Order of the 29th of January. That is nearly two months before the date of the 23rd of April. The parties met and discussed. Prior to this Status Conference, we have a footnote 4 of the Scheduling Order which deals with the Appeals Chamber practice, which is want to put questions prior to the hearing. We'd like it know, on behalf of the two parties, whether the Appeals Chamber plans to put questions in writing to them; and in the affirmative, could we have the written questions, say, four weeks, a month, before the hearing, so that we can prepare ourselves and thereby assisting the Appeals Chamber in the best way possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. In respect of your question of written questions from the Appeals Chamber addressed to the parties, I wish to say that if the Appeals Chamber should decide to put specific questions to the parties on parts of their respective appeals briefs, it will be done at least three to four weeks before the date of the hearing. In this way, you will be able to prepare yourselves, of course. This won't preclude the Appeals Judges from asking other questions in order to seek clarifications on your submissions at the hearing itself. Do you have any further questions, now turning to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what my learned friend stated -- from the Prosecution stated also represented our position, and we have no additional requests. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, too. Now, in the absence of any further questions, the Status Conference stands adjourned. Thank you all. Have a good afternoon.
